authoring: Source-reviewed before any extractor/retrieval/model outputs; independent semantic review required before inference.
target_groups_semantics: OR within each group, AND across all groups. Assigned-function/member symbols use their assignment name; named callbacks use their source name; nested names use dot qualification.

queries.query: Where is request-header lookup validated and made case-insensitive, while treating the two spellings of the referring-page header as aliases?
queries.notes: The chained get/header assignment shares one implementation, validates name, lowercases it, and checks referrer/referer. Either source alias is equivalent.

queries.query: Where is JSON wrapped in a browser callback only when a nonempty callback string exists, with callback-name characters restricted and Unicode line separators escaped?
queries.notes: First array callback value is selected; callbacks are filtered, Unicode separators escaped, and output guarded by typeof with the existing mitigation prefix.

queries.query: Where are response-cookie values serialized, optionally signed using a required request secret, and millisecond lifetimes converted into expiry dates and whole-second maximum ages?
queries.notes: Copies options, encodes object values with j:, signs s: values, converts age, defaults path, and appends serialized Set-Cookie; this is signing, not encryption.

queries.query: Where is a cookie cleared by forcing an expiry in the past and discarding a supplied maximum age before emitting an empty value?
queries.notes: The helper creates a fresh options object, overrides expires, removes maxAge, and delegates to cookie. Normal cookie lifetime logic is a decoy.

queries.query: Where is an outgoing header appended without replacing existing values, handling scalar and array values on either side?
queries.notes: Reads the previous header, concatenates combinations, then uses set for serialization. Header replacement itself is not sufficient.

queries.query: Where are response formats selected from acceptable content types, varying on Accept and calling a default handler or forwarding a 406 error when none match?
queries.notes: Filters default from negotiable keys, asks req.accepts, sets content type for a match, and uses default or createError406 with normalized types.

queries.query: Where is a redirect response generated with negotiated plain-text or escaped HTML content and its byte length, while suppressing the body for a header-only request?
queries.notes: Location is set first, format chooses the body, HTML escapes address, Content-Length uses byteLength, HEAD ends without body. The helper accepts optional status/url arguments.

queries.query: Where are nested applications mounted as middleware and the parent request/response prototypes restored before continuation after the child application finishes?
queries.notes: The app-like branch records parent/mountpath, delegates child handle, restores orig.request/orig.response, forwards err, and emits mount.

queries.query: Where is the configured simple, extended, custom, or disabled query parser compiled and then invoked on the raw URL query, with disabled parsing returning an empty object?
queries.notes: All layers required: setting compilation trigger, mode-to-function selection, and request getter invocation. Parsing algorithm inside external qs/querystring is outside scope.

queries.query: Where is a proxy-trust policy compiled from a boolean, hop count, address list, or custom function, then used to decide whether the forwarded protocol header may override the socket protocol?
queries.notes: Setting compiles trust; compileTrust supports custom/true/hop count/comma lists and external address compiler; protocol uses trust(remoteAddress,0), then first forwarded token. External proxyaddr internals are outside scope.

queries.query: Where are template render options merged and cached views reused, while uncached views are searched across configured roots using both the direct filename and a directory index filename?
queries.notes: App render merges locals and manages cache/lookup errors; View.lookup walks roots; View.resolve tries file and index.ext. External template engine execution is not gold for this query.

queries.query: Where is a callable HTTP application created with its own request and response prototypes, and where are those prototypes installed on incoming objects with cross-references and per-response local state before routing?
queries.notes: Factory returns a listener calling app.handle and builds app-specific prototypes. handle sets cross-references, installs prototypes, creates null-prototype locals, then delegates router.

queries.query: Where does the framework enforce a built-in per-client-IP token-bucket rate limit and emit a retry-after header when the bucket is exhausted?
queries.notes: Scoped absent: production lib dispatches user middleware and interprets proxy trust, but has no built-in rate limiter/token-bucket storage. Applications or separate middleware may supply one.

absence_review.scope: All pinned production source within declared source_root and exclusions; dependencies, examples, tests, and user plugins are outside this claim.

closest_decoys.reason: Registers user middleware; does not impose request rates.

queries.query: Where are failed outbound HTTP requests retried with exponential backoff and a maximum attempt count?
queries.notes: Scoped absent: Express creates/dispatches an inbound HTTP server; no outbound request retry client is implemented within lib.

absence_review.scope: All pinned production source within declared source_root and exclusions; dependencies, examples, tests, and user plugins are outside this claim.

closest_decoys.reason: Creates an inbound server; does not send or retry outbound requests.

queries.query: Where are response cookies authenticated and encrypted with automatic key rotation rather than merely signed?
queries.notes: Scoped absent: cookie optionally signs a serialized value with the supplied secret. No encryption or rotation machinery is implemented in production lib.

closest_decoys.reason: Signing preserves serialized content; no encryption/key rotation.

source_evidence_scoring: A group is covered by any verified source window from the pinned file whose actual source bytes include the complete executable evidence span. Enclosing/nested/file windows are eligible irrespective of symbol label. One window can cover multiple required groups. Symbols alone never establish a hit.
